Official Line Item Title: NONTRADITIONAL 1-4 FAMILY RESIDENTIAL MORTGAGE LOANS
Official Line Item Definition: Report the balance sheet amount of nontraditional 1-4 family residential mortgage loans (in domestic offices); which include all 1-4 family residential loan products that allow the borrower to defer repayment of principal or interest and includes all interest-only products; teaser rate mortgages; and negative amortizing mortgages; with the exception of home equity lines of credit and reverse mortgages. Nontraditional 1-4 family residential mortgage loans should include simultaneous second lien loans and closed-end home equity loans to the extent such loans meet any of the characteristics described above. A teaser-rate mortgage loan is defined as a mortgage with a discounted initial rate where the lender offers a lower rate and lower payments for part of the mortgage term. A mortgage loan is no longer considered a nontraditional mortgage once the teaser rate has expired; or in the case of an escalating interest rate; once the rate is no longer discounted and the borrower is making full principal and interest payments (has not been granted any principal and interest concessions). Official Line Item Title: ADJUSTABLE RATE CLOSED-END LOANS SECURED BY FIRST LIENS ON 1-4 FAMILY RESIDENTIAL PROPERTIES
Official Line Item Definition: Includes the amount of closed-end loans secured by first liens on 1-to-4 family residential properties (in domestic offices) included in Schedule RC-C; item 5367 that have a floating or adjustable interest rate.    A floating or adjustable rate is a rate that varies; or can vary; in relation to an index; to some other interest rate such  as the rate on certain U.S. Government securities; or to some other variable criterion the exact value of which cannot be  known in advance. Therefore; the exact rate the loan carries at any subsequent time cannot be known at the time of  origination. For purposes of this item; even if the rate on a loan with a floating or adjustable rate can no longer float because it has reached a floor or ceiling level; the loan is to be reported in this item as an adjustable rate loan.    Also; amortizing fixed rate loans secured by first liens on 1-to-4 family residential properties that have original maturities of one year or less and require a balloon payment at maturity are included in this item.

The amount of recourse exposure reported should not include interest payments the bank has  advanced on delinquent loans. Official Line Item Definition: Report the total of:  The principal amount of closed-end first lien and junior lien 1-4 family residential mortgage loans sold during the calendar quarter ending on the report date; and The total amount of open-end commitments under revolving; open-end lines of credit secured by 1-4 family residential mortgage properties sold during the calendar quarter ending on the report date.  Include transfers of closed-end and open-end 1-4 family residential mortgage loans originated or purchased for resale from retail or wholesale sources that have been accounted for as sales in accordance with ASC Topic 860; Transfers and Servicing (formerly FASB Statement No. 140; 'Accounting for Transfers and Servicing of Financial Assets and Extinguishments of Liabilities;' as amended); i.e.; those transfers where the loans are no longer included in the bank's consolidated total assets. What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: 1-4 family residential mortgage loans held for sale or trading at quarter end
Official Line Item Definition: Report the total of: The carrying amount of closed-end first lien and junior lien 1-4 family residential mortgage loans held for sale or trading as of the quarter-end report date; and the total amount of open-end commitments under revolving; open-end lines of credit secured by 1-4 family residential properties held for sale or trading as of the quarter-end report date.  These closed-end loans and the funded amounts under these revolving; open-end lines of credit are included in Schedule RC; item 4.a; Loans and leases held for sale; and Schedule RC; item 5; Trading assets.  Closed-end loans held for sale should be reported at the lower of cost or fair value or at fair value consistent with their presentation in Schedule RC; item 4.a. Closed-end loans held for trading should be reported at fair value consistent with their presentation in Schedule RC; item 5. Closed-end and open-end 1-4 family residential mortgage loans held for sale or trading at quarter-end include any mortgage loans transferred at any time from the bank's loan portfolio to a held-for-sale account or a trading account that have not been sold by quarter-end.

Official Line Item Definition: Report the balance sheet amount of nontraditional 1-4 family residential mortgage loans (in domestic offices); which include all 1-4 family residential loan products that allow the borrower to defer repayment of principal or interest and includes all interest-only products; teaser rate mortgages; and negative amortizing mortgages; with the exception of home equity lines of credit and reverse mortgages. Nontraditional 1-4 family residential mortgage loans should include simultaneous second lien loans and closed-end home equity loans to the extent such loans meet any of the characteristics described above. A mortgage loan is no longer considered a nontraditional mortgage once the teaser rate has expired; or in the case of an escalating interest rate; once the rate is no longer discounted and the borrower is making full principal and interest payments (has not been granted any principal and interest concessions). Also includes loans and advances to investees and holdings of their bonds; notes; and debentures.    Investments in investees are reported using the equity method of accounting. Under the equity method the  carrying value of the bank's investment in an investee is originally recorded at cost but is adjusted periodically to record  as income the bank's proportionate share of the investees earnings or losses and decreased by the amount of any cash  dividends or similar distributions received from the investee. Official Line Item Definition: The sum of 'Total Transaction Accounts for Individuals; Partnerships; and Corporations (1919)'; 'Total  Transaction Accounts for Commercial Banks in the U.S. (Including IBF) (1931)'; 'Total Transaction Accounts for  Banks in Foreign Countries (1932)'; 'Total Transaction Accounts and Credit Balances for Foreign Governments and  Official Institutions (Including Foreign Central Banks) (1649)'; 'Total Transaction Accounts and Credit Balances - All  Other Deposits and Credit Balances (1650)' and 'Total Transaction Accounts and Credit Balances - Certified and Official Checks (2330)'.    NOTE:    Reported on the FR 2069 (WALB) report.    Excludes all transactions with related depository institutions.    Reported only by the FFIEC 002 reporters.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: COMMERCIAL AND ALL OTHER LOANS AND ALL LEASES - RESTRUCTURED
Official Line Item Definition: Includes commercial and all other loans and all leases that have been restructured and are in compliance with modified terms. Excludes loans to individuals for household; family; and other personal expenditures.   NOTE:   This item is reported by savings banks only.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL TRANSACTION ACCOUNTS AND CREDIT BALANCES FOR COMMERCIAL BANKS IN THE UNITED STATES (INCLUDING IBFS)
Official Line Item Definition: The sum of 'Total Transaction Accounts and Credit Balances of U.S. Branches and Agencies of Other Foreign Banks (1643)' and 'Total Transaction Accounts and Credit Balances of Other Commercial Banks in the U.S. (1645)'.  NOTE:  Reported as an derived item in Schedule E for the FFIEC 002 report.

What This Line Measures: Past-due, nonaccrual, or troubled loan status
Official Line Item Title: COMMERCIAL AND ALL OTHER LOANS AND ALL LEASES - PAST DUE 30 THROUGH 89 DAYS AND STILL ACCRUING
Official Line Item Definition: Includes the full outstanding balances of commercial and all other loans and all leases that are past due 30 through  89 days and upon which the bank continues to accrue interest. Also includes loans and leases that have been restructured by means of a modification of terms.   COMPARABILITY:    Prior to 6/30/86; excludes restructured loans; reported in 'Commercial and All Other Loans and All Leases - Renegotiated 'Troubled' Debt (1972)'.   NOTE:   This item is reported by savings banks only.

What This Line Measures: Past-due, nonaccrual, or troubled loan status
Official Line Item Title: COMMERCIAL AND ALL OTHER LOANS AND ALL LEASES - PAST DUE 90 DAYS OR MORE AND STILL ACCRUING
Official Line Item Definition: Includes the full outstanding balances of commercial and all other loans and all leases that are past due 90 days or  more and upon which the bank continues to accrue interest. Also includes loans and leases that have been restructured by means of a modification of terms.   COMPARABILITY:    Prior to 6/30/86; excludes restructured loans; reported in 'Commercial and All Other Loans and All Leases - Renegotiated 'Troubled' Debt (1972)'.   NOTE:   This item is reported by savings banks only.

What This Line Measures: Past-due, nonaccrual, or troubled loan status
Official Line Item Title: COMMERCIAL AND ALL OTHER LOANS AND ALL LEASES - NONACCRUAL
Official Line Item Definition: Includes the outstanding balances of commercial and all other loans and all leases that the bank has placed in  nonaccrual status. Also includes loans and leases that have been restructured by means of a modification of terms and that are in nonaccrual status.   COMPARABILITY:    Prior to 6/30/86; excludes restructured loans; reported in 'Commercial and All Other Loans and All Leases - Renegotiated 'Troubled' Debt (1972)'.   NOTE:   This item is reported by savings banks only.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: COMMERCIAL AND ALL OTHER LOANS AND ALL LEASES - RENEGOTIATED 'TROUBLED' DEBT
Official Line Item Definition: Includes the total of the outstanding balances of commercial and all other loans and all leases that have been  renegotiated to provide a reduction of either interest or principal because of a deterioration in the financial position of the borrower.   NOTE:   This item is reported by savings banks only.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: LOANS TO INDIVIDUALS FOR HOUSEHOLD; FAMILY; AND OTHER PERSONAL EXPENDITURES
Official Line Item Definition: Includes all loans; not secured primarily by real estate; to individuals for medical expenses; personal taxes;  vacations; consolidation of personal (nonbusiness) debts; for the purchase of private passenger automobiles; household  appliances; furniture; mobile homes; trailers; boats; etc.; and loans not secured primarily by real estate for the purpose of purchasing real estate that will be used as a residence of the borrower's family.    Includes demand loans; installment loans; and single-payment time loans; regardless of size or maturity and  regardless of whether the loans are made by the personal loan department or any other department of the bank. Includes  all credit extended to individuals through retail (charge account) credit card plans; and loans arising from bank check  credit; other revolving credit; special overdraft credit; or similar plans. Includes retail installment sales paper purchased  by the bank from dealers; finance companies; and others. However; excludes loans made to dealers and finance  companies on their own promissory notes; secured by the pledge of installment paper. Loans to dealers are included in  'Commercial and Industrial Loans (1600)'

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: LOANS TO PURCHASE PRIVATE PASSENGER AUTOMOBILES ON INSTALLMENT BASIS
Official Line Item Definition: Includes the outstanding amount of  loans to individuals. Includes both direct loans and indirect loans (purchased  paper) arising from the retail sale of private passenger automobiles; whether or not the loan is collateralized by the  automobile.  Also; includes loans to purchase light trucks for personal use; such as pickup trucks; vans; minivans; and sport-utility vehicles.     Excludes  loans for the purpose of purchasing motorcycles; travel trailers; campers and similar recreational vehicles.       Does not include loans arising from the retail sale of commercial vehicles and taxicabs; which are reported in  'Commercial and Industrial Loans (1600)'; or loans arising from the retail sale of farm equipment; which is reported in  'Loans to Finance Agricultural Production and Other Loans to Farmers (1590)' or 'Commercial and Industrial Loans (1600)'; as appropriate. Reported net of hypothecated deposits.    NOTE:    Reported for the FR 2571 (CNCR).    COMPARABILITY:     Prior to 9/30/1997; included loans on an installment basis and excluded loans to purchase light trucks for  personal use; such as pickup truck

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: LOANS TO PURCHASE OTHER RETAIL GOODS ON INSTALLMENT BASIS - MOBILE HOMES
Official Line Item Definition: Includes both direct loans and indirect loans (purchased paper) arising from the sale to individuals of new or used  private mobile homes; whether or not the mobile home is used as collateral. Mobile homes are defined as complete  dwelling units built on a chassis and capable at the time of initial purchase of being towed over the highway by truck but  not by car. Excludes loans to purchase travel trailers; campers; and similar recreation vehicles. Excludes 'floor plan'  loans or other wholesale financing of loans to purchase mobile homes for business or professional purposes which are  reported in 'Commercial and Industrial Loans.' Excludes loans to farmers and loans secured by real estate. Reported net of hypothecated deposits.    COMPARABILITY:    Prior to 3/31/79; only the CNCR series was reported net of hypothecated deposits.    Prior to 6/30/71; not shown separately but included in 'Loans to Purchase Other Retail Goods on Installment Basis - Other Retail Consumer Goods (2040)'.

What This Line Measures: Total loans or portfolio-level aggregate
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL LOANS AND LEASES; NET OF UNEARNED INCOME
Official Line Item Definition: Beginning 6/30/1997; excludes holdings of commercial paper which are now reported as securities for the FR Y-11Q (BHCS) and FR Y-9SP (BHSP) report. For the FR Y-11Q (BHCS) report; also excludes the fair value of any assets received in full or partial satisfaction of a loan or lease (unless the asset received is itself reportable as a loan or lease) and any loans for which the nonbank subsidiary has obtained physical possession of the underlying collateral regardless of whether formal foreclosure or repossession proceedings have been instituted against the borrower.     Beginning 3/31/94; reported on Schedule J; by all banking Edge corporations and all banking agreement corporations that have branch offices (RCF0 thru RCF9); for the FR 2886B report. Prior to 3/31/84; excludes 'Lease Financing Receivables (2165)'.       NOTE:     For the FR Y-9C Schedule HC-I--Risk-Based Capital report; includes loans and lease financing receivables reported in item BHCK2122 on Schedule HC-B. The mnemonic prefixes for the risk weight columns represents the following:     BHC0 = (Column A) 0%   BHC2 = (Column B) 20%   BHC5 = (Column C) 50%

What This Line Measures: Charge-offs, recoveries, or provision for loan losses
Official Line Item Title: INVESTMENTS AND UNCONSOLIDATED SUBSIDIARIES AND ASSOCIATED COMPANIES
Official Line Item Definition: Includes the amount of the bank's investments in subsidiaries that have not been consolidated; associated  companies; and corporate joint ventures; unincorporated joint ventures; general partnerships; and limited partnerships  over which the bank exercises significant influence (collectively referred to as 'investees'). Also includes loans and advances to investees and holdings of their bonds; notes; and debentures.    Investments in investees are reported using the equity method of accounting. Under the equity method the  carrying value of the bank's investment in an investee is originally recorded at cost but is adjusted periodically to record  as income the bank's proportionate share of the investees earnings or losses and decreased by the amount of any cash  dividends or similar distributions received from the investee. For the purposes of the FFIEC 031; 032; 033; 034 reports;  the date through which the carrying value of the bank's investment in an investee has been adjusted should; to the extent  practicable; match the report date of the Report of Condition; but in no case differ by more than 93 days from the report date. What This Line Measures: Supplemental memorandum or supporting detail
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL ASSETS HELD IN TRADING ACCOUNTS
Official Line Item Definition: This item is a duplicate of 3545. Item 3545 should be used where feasible.  Includes the value of all assets held in the bank's trading accounts. All assets held in trading accounts are to be  reported consistently at market value or the lower of cost or market value. Assets held in trading accounts includes but are  not limited to: (1) U.S. Treasury securities; (2) U.S. Government Agency and Corporation obligations; (3) securities  issued by states and political subdivisions in the U.S.; (4) other bonds; notes; and debentures; (5) certificates of deposit; (6) commercial paper; and (7) bankers acceptances.  Excludes the carrying value of any debt securities; loans; or leases that are held for sale. Debt securities held for  sale are reported in Schedule RC-B (including Memorandum item 5356) and in Schedule RC; item 0390. Loans and leases held for sale are reported in Schedule RC-C (including Memorandum item 5369) and in Schedule RC; item 2122.  NOTE:  Reported on the Balance Sheet for the FR Y-7 (FNBK) report. Reported only by nonbank subsidiaries with total assets of more than $150 million.  For the FR Y-9C (BHCK) report; the MDRM reflects data starting for the period of June 30;

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: CUSTOMERS' LIABILITY TO THIS BANK ON ACCEPTANCES OUTSTANDING
Official Line Item Definition: Includes the liability to the reporting bank of its customers on drafts and bills of exchange which have been  accepted by the reporting bank or by other banks for its account and which are outstanding; i.e.; not held by the bank on  date of condition report. If held by the reporting bank; they are reported as loans and discounts. In case a customer  anticipated his liability to the bank on outstanding acceptances by paying the bank either full amount of his liability or  any part thereof in advance of actual maturity of the acceptance; the bank decreases the amount of customer's liability on  outstanding acceptance. If such funds are not received for immediate application to reduction of the indebtedness to the  bank or the receipt thereof does not immediately reduce or extinguish the indebtedness; then such funds held to meet  acceptance are reported in demand deposits. Amount reported here does not include customers' liability on unused  commercial and travelers' letters of credit issued under guaranty or against the deposit of security; i.e.; not issued for money or its equivalent. What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: DEPOSITS WITH AFFILIATED COMMERCIAL BANKS IN THE U.S.
Official Line Item Definition: Includes all balances representing deposits or placements with affiliated commercial banks in the U.S. Also includes correspondent; reciprocal or operating balances.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: OTHER BALANCES WITH AFFILIATES
Official Line Item Definition: All other claims on affiliates including subordinated debt. Excludes equity claims and deposits with U.S. commercial banks.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: CLAIMS ON AFFILIATES
Official Line Item Definition: The sum of 'Stock and Other Equity Interests in Affiliates (2172)'; 'Deposits With Affiliated Commercial Banks in the U.S. (2173)' and 'Other Balances With Affiliates (2174)'.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL TRANSACTION ACCOUNTS - ALL OTHER DEPOSITS
Official Line Item Definition: Includes all deposits of banks located in foreign countries and of foreign governments and official institutions  (including foreign central banks). Banks in foreign countries includes: (1) foreign-domiciled branches of other U.S.  banks; and (2) foreign-domiciled branches of foreign banks. All reciprocal balances; including demand balances; with banks in foreign countries and with foreign central banks should be reported gross in this item.    Excludes U.S. branches and agencies of foreign banks and of foreign official banking institutions; New York  State Investment Companies (chartered under Article XII of the New York State Banking Code) that perform a banking  business and that are majority-owned by one or more foreign banks; and foreign government-owned nonbank commercial and industrial enterprises. (See item 2201 for the term 'transaction accounts.')  COMPARABILITY:  Beginning 3/31/01; reported as a derived item for the FFIEC 041 report.  Reported on Schedule RC-E.  NOTE:   Reported as a derived item for the FFIEC 031; 032 and 033 reports which includes the sum of items 2213 and 2216.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL DEPOSITS OF COMMERCIAL BANKS IN THE U.S. (SEE NOTE BELOW)
Official Line Item Definition: Includes the total of all 'Transaction Deposits of Commercial Banks in the U.S. (2206)' and 'Nontransaction Deposits of Commercial Banks in the U.S. (2550)'.  NOTE:   Reported as an derived item for the FR 2886B report; as RCON2188 which includes RCON2206 plus RCON2550.  COMPARABILITY:   Prior to 3/31/94; reported as an derived item for the FR 2886B report; as RCFD2188 which included the  sum of RCFN2188 plus RCON2206 and plus RCON2550. Also as RCFN2188 which included the sum of RCFN2206 and RCFN2550.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL DEPOSITS
Official Line Item Definition: Includes the sum of 'Total Transaction Accounts (2215)'; plus 'Nontransaction Savings Deposits (2389)'; plus 'Total Time Deposits (2514))'.     Total deposits as defined by the Federal Deposit Insurance Act are:     (1) Unpaid balance of money or its equivalent received or held by a bank in the usual course of business and for which it has given or is obligated to give credit; either conditionally or unconditionally; to a commercial; checking; savings; time; or thrift account; or which is evidenced by its certificate of deposit; or a check or draft drawn against a deposit account and certified by the bank; or a letter of credit or a traveler's check on which the bank is primarily liable: provided that without limiting the generality of 'money or its equivalent;' any such account or instrument must be regarded as evidencing receipt of the equivalent of money when credited or issued in exchange for checks; drafts; or a promissory note upon which the person obtaining any such credit or instrument is primarily or secondarily liable; or for a charge against a deposit account; or in settlement of checks; drafts; or other instruments forwarded to such bank for collecti

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL TRANSACTION ACCOUNTS - DEPOSITS OF INDIVIDUALS; PARTNERSHIPS; AND CORPORATIONS
Official Line Item Definition: The term 'transaction account' is defined as a deposit or account on which the depositor or account holder is  permitted to make withdrawals by negotiable or transferable instrument; payment orders of withdrawal; telephone transfers; or other similar devices for the purpose of making payments or transfers to third persons or others.  Includes:   (1)   Deposits related to the personal; household; or family activities of both farm and nonfarm individuals and to the business activities of sole proprietorships;  (2)   Deposits of corporations and organizations (other than depository institutions); regardless of whether or not they are operated for profit; including but not limited to: (a) mutual funds and other nondepository financial institutions; (b) foreign government-owned nonbank commercial and industrial enterprises; and (c) quasi-governmental organizations such as post exchanges on military posts and deposits of a company; battery; or similar organization (unless the reporting bank has been designated by the U.S. Treasury as a depository for such funds and appropriate security for the deposits has been pledged; in which case; include in item 2202);  (3)   Dealer reserve accounts

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL TRANSACTION ACCOUNTS - DEPOSITS OF COMMERCIAL BANKS IN THE U.S.
Official Line Item Definition: Excludes deposits of IBFs; building or savings and loan associations; homestead associations; cooperative  banks; credit unions; and mutual or stock savings banks and banks in foreign countries. (See item 2201 for the term 'transaction accounts'.)   NOTE:   Reported as a separate item for the FR 2886B report.    Includes all transaction accounts of commercial banks located in the U.S. Commercial banks in the U.S.  includes: (1) U.S. branches and agencies of foreign banks; and (2) all other commercial banks in the U.S.; i.e.; U.S.  branches of U.S. banks. For purposes of these reports; U.S. branches and agencies of foreign banks includes U.S.  branches and agencies of foreign official banking institutions and investment companies that are chartered under Article  XII of the New York State Banking Law and that are majority-owned by one or more foreign banks. Reciprocal demand balances with the banking institutions listed above should be reported net in this item.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL TRANSACTION ACCOUNTS - DEPOSITS OF OTHER DEPOSITORY INSTITUTIONS IN THE U.S.
Official Line Item Definition: Includes all deposits of depository institutions in the U.S. other than commercial banks. Includes deposits of  building or savings and loan associations; homestead associations; and cooperative banks; mutual and stock savings  banks; and credit unions. Reciprocal demand balances with the depository institutions listed above should be reported gross in this item. (See item 2201 for the term 'transaction accounts'.)

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL TRANSACTION ACCOUNTS
Official Line Item Definition: Includes the sum of 'Deposits of Individuals; Partnerships; and Corporations (2201)'; 'Deposits of U.S.  Government (2202)'; 'Deposits of States and Political Subdivisions in the U.S. (2203)'; 'Deposits  of Commercial  Banks in the U.S. (2206)'; 'Deposits of Other Depository Institutions in the U.S. (2207)'; 'Deposits of Banks in Foreign  Countries (2213)'; 'Deposits of Foreign Governments and Official Institutions (Including Foreign Central Banks) (2216)' and 'Certified and Official Checks (2330)'. What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: DEMAND DEPOSITS OF INDIVIDUALS; PARTNERSHIPS; AND CORPORATIONS
Official Line Item Definition: The total of 'Demand Deposits of Mutual Savings Banks (2230)'; 'Demand Deposits of Savings and Loan Associations (2235)' and 'Demand Deposits of Other Individuals; Partnerships; and Corporations (2240).'    NOTE:     For the  FFIEC 002 report; reported as an derived item in Schedule E which includes the sum of items 2223 and 2224.     For the Quarterly Report of Condition for New York State Investment Companies; includes amounts for credit balances; which are reported separately on the IBA Call.    COMPARABILITY:     Beginning 12/31/73; national banks includes deposits of U.S. postmasters of government funds which have  come into their possession by virtue of their official positions. Prior to 4/12/61: (1) excludes 'Demand Deposits of Mutual Savings Banks (2230)' which is included in  'Demand Deposits of Commercial Banks in the U.S. (2310)'; (2) includes a small portion of 'Demand  Deposits of Foreign Governments and Official Institutions; Central Banks; and International Institutions (2300)'.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: DEMAND DEPOSITS OF MUTUAL SAVINGS BANKS
Official Line Item Definition: Includes all demand deposits of mutual savings banks domiciled in the United States; Puerto Rico; and U.S. territories and possessions.    COMPARABILITY:     Prior to 4/12/61; not shown separately but included in 'Demand Deposits of Commercial Banks in the U.S. (2310).'

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TRANSACTION ACCOUNTS - DEPOSITS AND CREDIT BALANCES OF COMMERCIAL BANKS IN THE UNITED STATES
Official Line Item Definition: Includes all transaction accounts of commercial banks in the United States. For purposes of the FR 2886a report;  a commercial bank in the U.S. is an individual; partnership; corporation or any other legal entity chartered as a  commercial bank and/or trust company by a unit of government in the U.S. or engaged in banking as a private or industrial  bank; and located in the U.S. (excluding any foreign branches thereof). Also includes; if not specified separately; U.S.  Agencies and Branches of Foreign Banks; Edge and Agreement Corporations (excluding any foreign branches thereof);  IBFs; and other investment companies chartered by the state of New York that are majority-owned by one or more foreign banks and are engaged in banking.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: NONTRANSACTION ACCOUNTS - DEPOSITS AND CREDIT BALANCES OF COMMERCIAL BANKS IN THE UNITED STATES
Official Line Item Definition: Includes all nontransaction accounts of commercial banks in the United States.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: ALL OTHER DEMAND DEPOSITS
Official Line Item Definition: The sum of 'Demand Deposits of Foreign Governments and Official Institutions (2300)'; 'Demand Deposits of Commercial Banks in the U.S. (2310)'; and 'Demand Deposits of Banks in Foreign Countries (2320)'.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: DEMAND DEPOSITS OF COMMERCIAL BANKS IN THE UNITED STATES
Official Line Item Definition: Includes all demand deposits standing to the credit of banks in the United States; Puerto Rico; and in U.S.  dependencies and insular possessions (including trust territories). 'Banks' includes national banks; state commercial  banks; trust companies performing a commercial banking business; industrial banks; private banks (including regulated  certificated banks) performing a commercial banking business; Edge Act and Agreement Corporations performing a  commercial banking business; and branches and agencies of foreign banks that are located in the United States; Puerto Rico; or U.S. dependencies and possessions.     Excludes deposits of international banking institutions; mutual savings banks; stock savings banks; building or  savings and loan and similar associations; the Export-Import Bank; cooperative banks; credit unions; federal lending agencies such as Federal Land Banks; Federal Intermediate Credit Banks; and Federal Home Loan Banks.     Also excludes banks in foreign countries. Reciprocal demand balances with the banking institutions listed above  are reported net. What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: DEMAND DEPOSITS OF U.S. BRANCHES AND AGENCIES OF FOREIGN BANKS
Official Line Item Definition: Includes demand deposits of U.S. branches and agencies of foreign banks and demand deposits of  U.S.-domiciled offices of New York State Article XII Investment Companies that are majority-owned by one or more foreign banks.    U.S. branches and agencies of foreign banks includes U.S.-domiciled branches and agencies of: (1) banks in  foreign countries; and (2) foreign official institutions. Foreign official banking institutions includes central banks and  nationalized banking and other banking institutions owned by foreign governments that have as an important part of their function activities similar to those of a central bank.     Reciprocal demand balances with these banking institutions are reported gross. Excludes demand deposits of  U.S.-chartered banks owned by foreign banks or by foreign official institutions (reported in 'Demand Deposits of Other Commercial Banks in the U.S. (2316)').   NOTE:   Reported only by banks with foreign offices.   For the FFIEC 002 report; excludes all transactions with related depository institutions.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: DEMAND DEPOSITS OF OTHER COMMERCIAL BANKS IN THE U.S.
Official Line Item Definition: Reported here are demand deposits of other U.S. -domiciled offices of commercial banks. For the purposes of  this item; banks include national banks; state-chartered commercial banks; trust companies performing a commercial  banking business; industrial banks; stock savings banks; private banks (including regulated certificated banks)  performing a commercial banking business; and Edge Act and Agreement Corporations that are domiciled in the United  States; Puerto Rico; or U.S. dependencies and possessions. Included here; then; are U.S.-chartered banks owned by  foreign banks of foreign official banking institutions (but not their U.S.-domiciled branches and agencies; which are reported in 'Demand Deposits of U.S. Branches and Agencies of Foreign Banks (2313)').   Reciprocal demand balances of these commercial banks are reported net.   NOTE:   Reported only by  banks with foreign offices.   For the FFIEC 002 report; excludes all transactions with related depository institutions.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: FEDERAL FUNDS PURCHASED AND SECURITIES SOLD UNDER AGREEMENTS TO REPURCHASE WITH OTHER COMMERCIAL BANKS IN THE U.S.
Official Line Item Definition: NOTE:   For purposes of the reporting branch or agency's IBF; other commercial banks in the U.S. includes: (1) IBFs  of nonrelated banking institutions other than IBFs of U.S. branches and agencies of foreign banks; and (2) nonrelated U.S. and foreign banks domiciled in Puerto Rico and the U.S. territories and possessions.  Reported only by FFIEC 002 reporters.    Includes all federal funds and securities transactions as defined in 'Federal Funds Purchased and Securities Sold  Under Agreements to Repurchase (2800)' with U.S. offices of nonrelated banking institutions domiciled in any state of the United States; the District of Columbia; Puerto Rico; and U.S. territories and possessions.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: DEMAND DEPOSITS OF OTHER BANKS IN FOREIGN COUNTRIES
Official Line Item Definition: Reported here are all demand deposits of foreign-domiciled commercial banks; savings banks; discount houses;  and other similar foreign-domiciled institutions that accept short term deposits. Includes deposits of foreign-domiciled  banking subsidiaries of both other U.S. banks and Edge Act and Agreement Corporations that are not owned by the  reporting bank. Also includes foreign-domiciled banking institutions that have U.S. branches and agencies; but excludes  the deposits of their U.S. branches and agencies (reported in 'Deposits of U.S. Branches and Agencies of Foreign Banks (2313)').   NOTE:   Reported only by banks with foreign offices.   For the FFIEC 002 report; excludes all transactions with related depository institutions.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL NONTRANSACTION ACCOUNTS - OTHER COMMERCIAL BANKS IN THE U.S.
Official Line Item Definition: Includes all nontransaction accounts of U.S. -domiciled branches of commercial banks in the U.S. other than U.S. branches and agencies of foreign banks. (see item 2346 for the term 'nontransaction accounts'.)    NOTE:   For the FFIEC 002 report; excludes all transactions with related depository institutions.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL NONTRANSACTION ACCOUNTS - DEPOSITS OF OTHER DEPOSITORY INSTITUTIONS IN THE U.S.
Official Line Item Definition: Includes all nontransaction accounts of depository institutions in the U.S. other than commercial banks. (See item 2346 for the term 'nontransaction accounts'.)

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TOTAL NONTRANSACTION ACCOUNTS - OTHER BANKS IN FOREIGN COUNTRIES
Official Line Item Definition: Includes all nontransaction accounts of foreign-domiciled commercial banks; savings banks; discount houses;  and other similar foreign-domiciled institutions that accept deposits. Also includes deposits of foreign-domiciled  banking subsidiaries (but not branches) of both other U.S. banks and Edge and Agreement Corporations that are not owned by the reporting bank. (See item 2346 for the term 'nontransaction accounts'.)   NOTE:   For the FFIEC 002 report; excludes all transactions with related depository institutions.

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type
Official Line Item Title: TIME DEPOSITS OF MUTUAL SAVINGS BANKS
Official Line Item Definition: Includes all time deposits standing to the credit of mutual savings banks domiciled in the United States; Puerto Rico; and U.S. territories and possessions.    COMPARABILITY:     Prior to 4/12/61; not shown separately but included in 'Time Deposits of Commercial Banks in the United States (2550).'

What This Line Measures: Outstanding loan balance by product type

Official Line Item Definition: Includes the dollar amount of the bank's fixed rate time deposits (i.e.; time certificates of deposit and open-account time deposits) of less than $100;000 with remaining maturities of three months or less.    A fixed interest rate is a rate that is specified at the origination of the transaction; is fixed and invariable during the  term of the time deposit; and is known to both the bank and the rate that changes during the term of the time deposit on a  predetermined basis; with the exact rate of interest over the life of the time deposit known with certainty to both the bank and the depositor when the time deposit is acquired. What This Line Measures: Loan maturity or interest-rate repricing bucket
Official Line Item Title: FLOATING RATE TIME DEPOSITS OF LESS THAN $100;000 WITH A REPRICING FREQUENCY OF QUARTERLY OR MORE FREQUENTLY
Official Line Item Definition: Includes the dollar amount of the bank's floating rate time deposits (i.e.; time certificates of deposit and  open-account time deposits) of less than $100;000 which can be repriced quarterly or more frequently (e.g.; quarterly; monthly; weekly; daily).    A floating rate is a rate that varies; or can vary; in relation to an index; to some other interest rate such as the rate on  certain U.S. Government securities or the bank's 'prime rate;' or to some other variable criterion the exact value of which  cannot be known in advance. Therefore; the exact rate the time deposit carries at any subsequent time cannot be known at the time the time deposit is received by the bank or subsequently renewed.    When the rate on a time deposit with a floating rate can no longer float because it has reached a floor or ceiling  level; the time deposit is to be treated as 'fixed rate' rather than as 'floating rate' until the rate is again free to float.   NOTE:    Reported in Schedule RC-E; Part I by commercial banks for the FFIEC 031; 032; 033; and 034 reports. Excludes savings banks.

Official Line Item Title: LOANS SECURED BY OWNER OCCUPIED NONFARM NONRESIDENTIAL PROPERTIES
Official Line Item Definition: Report the amount of loans secured by owner-occupied nonfarm nonresidential properties included in Schedule RC-C; part I; item 1.e.    Loans secured by owner-occupied nonfarm nonresidential properties' are those nonfarm nonresidential property loans for which the primary source of repayment is the cash flow from the ongoing operations and activities conducted by the party; or an affiliate of the party; who owns the property. Thus; for loans secured by owner-occupied nonfarm nonresidential properties; the primary source of repayment is not derived from third party; nonaffiliated; rental income associated with the property (i.e.; any such rental income is less than 50 percent of the source of repayment) or the proceeds of the sale; refinancing; or permanent financing of the property. Include loans secured by hospitals; golf courses; recreational facilities; and car washes unless the property is owned by an investor who leases the property to the operator who; in turn; is not related to or affiliated with the investor. Also include loans secured by churches unless the property is owned by an investor who leases the property to the congregation.    Note:  &#x0D
